Diego Da Rin of the International Crisis Group described his organization to AP as one of Haiti's most structured criminal groups with significant territorial control. The strike followed Salvadoran forces attacking the residence of Wilson Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, on November 8; the two leaders were allies and are considered among the capital's main criminal bosses.

Bukele deployed about 2,500 troops to Haiti last month after four Salvadoran soldiers were attacked on October 18 in gang-controlled territory and went missing. Thousands of Haitians took to the streets of Port-au-Prince for a second consecutive day to celebrate the operation, with vendor Mario Jean-Pierre stating that Jeff is a criminal he hopes is dead and crediting Bukele for answering their request for help. Experts warn that while helicopters and explosive drones have intensified operations against criminal organizations, they have also increased risk to civilians, noting that maintaining control of retaken territories and preventing gang reprisals against residents remains one of the main challenges.
items.title: Bukele confirms airstrike on Haitian gang leader Jeff's mansion

items.summary: Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said Wednesday that Russian President Vladimir Putin, US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping will decide for themselves how long their trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen will last. Speaking to reporters at the event, Ushakov noted that Russia, the US and China have already agreed on the composition of the delegations participating in the talks. He said the leaders would decide how much time to spend discussing their issues and added that the meeting could run longer than the one hour allocated under protocol. "The leaders will decide themselves how much time to spend discussing the issues," Ushakov said, adding that if the discussion engages all three leaders no one could stop them, not even the protocol service. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had earlier stated the trilateral meeting was scheduled to last no more than an hour. On a separate matter, Ushakov said Putin and Trump are also due to hold bilateral talks after the summit's plenary session, with several members of each delegation present; he described preparations as underway and expressed hope that the meeting would be useful and substantive. Commenting on Putin's closed-door conversation with Xi Jinping, Ushakov said key international and regional issues were discussed, including the conflict in Ukraine and the latest round of negotiations in Abu Dhabi. He characterized the exchange as a continuation of their regular dialogue, noting they spoke openly and frankly, and described it as both substantive and useful for both sides. When asked about Putin's other contacts at the summit reception, Ushakov said he had briefly spoken with several APEC leaders including Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto, and that further contacts could occur during the following day's program. Addressing criticism from former US Secretary of State Hillary Clinton, who warned a Trump-Putin-Xi trilateral meeting would damage the US image, Ushakov dismissed it by saying "Perhaps it damages Clinton's image," while asserting that the current US president sets his own agenda and decides what serves his country's interests. He also said it was too early to determine whether Putin would attend the G20 Leaders' Summit in Doral, Florida on Dec. 14 and 15, adding a decision was unlikely to be made on Nov. 18 or 19.
items.title: Kremlin Says Putin, Trump and Xi Will Set Their Own Meeting Duration

items.summary: Apple has rolled out an upgraded Apple Maps experience in India, introducing several new navigation features aimed at making travel easier for users there. According to GSM Arena, the update brings Natural Language Guidance, which provides more conversational directions and incorporates real-world landmarks and points of interest to help users navigate. The app now also features more than 300 three-dimensional landmarks across India. A blog post shared by Apple describes Lane Guidance as a feature that helps users navigate lanes more effectively, alongside multi-stop routing that lets them plan journeys with multiple destinations. Dual-language labels have been added to reflect the use of English and regional languages on Indian road signs. Language support has expanded to include Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Punjabi, Odia and Urdu for Indian users. The update also adds a Share ETA feature that lets users share their estimated time of arrival with friends and family. Look Around now offers new street-level imagery giving users a closer view of locations, while additional features include augmented reality step-by-step walking directions, cycling directions, custom route creation and preferred routes. The article was published on November 19, 2026.
items.title: Apple Maps India update adds lane guidance and multi-stop routing

items.summary:
Anthropic priced its initial public offering at $83 a share, above its targeted range of $70 to $78 per share on Wednesday. The sale is one of the largest stock-market IPOs on record and the first by a major frontier artificial intelligence model developer. Anthropic initially planned to sell 825 million shares, though the size of the offering has increased according to an unidentified source who requested not be identified because the information isn't public.

The listing is the second mega-IPO this year focused on AI, following SpaceX's sale in June, as investors seek exposure to the fast-growing industry even amid mounting questions about the cost of developing and operating artificial intelligence models. The pricing followed a roadshow that attracted demand several times the number of shares offered, despite concerns about Anthropic's outlook and its ability to sustain rapid growth as competition intensifies.

Anthropic declined to comment on the offering. Bloomberg News first reported on the pricing, and shares are expected to start trading on Nasdaq Thursday under the ticker ANT. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley serve as lead underwriters in a 22-bank syndicate; both banks also led SpaceX's IPO earlier this year.

Anthropic's growth has been driven by surging demand for its Claude models, particularly Claude Code, its coding agent popular among software developers. Its annualized revenue run rate reached $81 billion as of October 31, up $10 billion from September 30 according to its IPO filing. The company reported it had 11,900 customers generating at least $100,000 in annual revenue on a trailing 12-month basis as of September 30, compared with more than 1,500 at the end of last year.

Sustaining that growth is becoming expensive. Anthropic spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, nearly four times the amount spent a year earlier, and incurred an additional $5 billion in computing costs in the third quarter, weighing on efficiency and reducing revenue generated per dollar of computing capacity. Revenue rose 47% in the third quarter to $16.96 billion.

The company reported an operating loss of $567 million compared with operating income of $974 million in the second quarter. Net loss fell to $23.3 billion from $66.3 billion a quarter earlier, including non-operating items related to bonds convertible into its shares. Anthropic has committed to nearly $900 billion in computing spending with infrastructure partners including Amazon and Alphabet's Google.

Its spending commitments expose the company to risks beyond its own finances. Anthropic warned in its prospectus that some of its computing providers depend on third-party financing and credit support to acquire chips and build capacity, adding that if such financing becomes unavailable or more costly, contracted capacity may be delayed, repriced, reduced, or not delivered. Investors have grown concerned about debt-fueled expansion of AI infrastructure as technology companies borrow heavily.

Anthropic also faces questions over how it will balance commercial ambitions with its emphasis on AI safety. CEO Dario Amodei has called for the industry to slow the pace of developing and releasing increasingly powerful models, warning that advances in AI could outstrip society's ability to manage the risks. Anthropic's closest rival, OpenAI, is also expected to pursue a public listing as early as next year.
items.title: Anthropic prices blockbuster AI IPO at $83 per share

items.summary: At The New York Times DealBook Summit on Wednesday, Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk publicly defended former Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang following his reported departure from the chipmaker. Speaking at the event, Musk questioned the decision to remove a leader tied to the company's success, describing Huang as one of the most talented entrepreneurs in history and an old friend. Comparing the situation to sports management, Musk said removing such a figure would be like "kicking Michael Jordan off your team" mid-season with a winning streak, calling it an unwise decision. He insisted he was not being inconsistent, stating, "You're not going to find me saying one thing publicly and another thing privately." Defending Huang against loyalty concerns, Musk said, "I don't think he's disloyal to the United States." Explaining why a replacement would be difficult, Musk highlighted Huang's operational experience and supplier relationships, noting that Huang eats street food in Korea and Taiwan with critical suppliers and has built long-term ties over decades. He added that many on Huang's team stayed out of personal loyalty despite higher offers elsewhere. When asked whether he would hire Huang himself, Musk responded affirmatively while clarifying that Huang was not seeking another job. Comparing the situation to a George R.R. Martin script with an unexpected plot twist, Musk expressed how shocking it is for such a central figure to suddenly disappear. According to the item, Huang co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and led it for over three decades, transforming it into an AI chipmaking powerhouse. His reported association with a woman suspected of links to Chinese intelligence has raised national security concerns, though the allegations remain unverified, placing Nvidia's leadership, governance, and China ties under renewed scrutiny.
items.title: Musk Defends Jensen Huang After Reported Nvidia Exit

items.summary: Anthropic raised a record $81.31 billion in its initial public offering, surpassing the previous benchmark of SpaceX's $75 billion fundraising and becoming the largest IPO ever. The San Francisco-based maker of the Claude AI tool priced its shares at $83 apiece on Wednesday, above its originally indicated range of $70-$78, valuing the company at $1.5 trillion. Investor demand was strong despite broader market uncertainties surrounding the technology sector and concerns about an AI bubble. The offering began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" starting Thursday. While Anthropic's initial plan had been to offer 825 million shares, the final deal comprised 980 million shares of Class A common stock: 956,351,354 sold by Anthropic itself and 23,648,646 offered by certain existing stockholders. Analyst Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. characterized the result as strong appetite for a major AI IPO and a big win for the tech sector after a difficult period involving Nvidia's leadership change. The article notes several market uncertainties at play, including the ouster of Nvidia's CEO, fears about an AI bubble, potential regulatory action by a Democratic-led Congress next year, and growing public anti-AI sentiment. Despite these factors, Anthropic's pricing signals that investors remain willing to fund major AI companies; its rival OpenAI is not planning to enter the stock market until next year. Beyond setting an IPO record, the fundraising lets Anthropic secure additional capital without increasing its debt burden. The company has already borrowed $6.2 billion, which it described as "substantial" in financial filings, and remains unprofitable under standard accounting rules, limiting resources available to service interest and principal payments. Its infrastructure commitments are significant: leases and other agreements will require spending $900 billion on computing power over the coming years, with $70 billion due within the next 12 months. Although Anthropic currently has ample cash reserves, its large spending plans could deplete those funds quickly if it cannot obtain additional financing.
items.title: Anthropic's Record $81.31 Billion IPO Surpasses SpaceX

items.summary:
At the New York Times' DealBook Summit, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk reaffirmed his public support for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, even as Nvidia's board shows no inclination to reinstate him. Comparing Huang's departure from a winning company to the Chicago Bulls dropping Michael Jordan during a championship run, Musk said he would not say one thing publicly and another privately, calling Huang an old friend and likening him to Michael Jordan at his peak in terms of what he means to a team. He argued that removing someone of Huang's calibre from a successful organization would be unwise, noting there is no replacement because Huang performs the roles of several people: managing supply chains while eating street food with critical suppliers in Korea and Taiwan, drawing on decades-long relationships. Musk also praised Huang's technological expertise and his strong employee loyalty, reporting that team members had declined better offers elsewhere due to their personal devotion to him. He stated he would readily hire Huang if the opportunity arose, describing him as one of the most talented entrepreneur CEOs in history and suggesting everyone else should want to do so as well. Musk added that Huang was probably still shocked by the developments, comparing the situation to a major character suddenly vanishing from a George R.R. Martin story.

In contrast, Nvidia's board appears firm against reinstating Huang. Board Chairman Harvey Jones has ruled out his return as CEO and announced a search for a permanent successor alongside the formation of a committee to strengthen oversight of national security policies and export control compliance. US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries also supports keeping Huang out, stating that any move to bring him back would be unacceptable on grounds of US national security and the risk of sensitive American technology being diverted to China. The dispute coincides with Huang's agreement to testify before three House committees on December 1 regarding his alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive accused of being a Chinese spy.
items.title: Musk Defends Jensen Huang Amid Nvidia Board's Reinstatement Resistance

items.summary: Indian gold loan lenders are seeking Reserve Bank of India approval to transfer stressed loans to asset reconstruction companies (ARCs), a move prompted by changes in repayment structures and a nearly 25% fall in gold prices over the past year. Industry officials support the ARC route, noting that while auctioning pledged jewellery helps recover dues, it can permanently deprive borrowers of assets representing generations of household savings. Under current rules, borrowers with higher loan-to-value ratios up to 75% must service interest monthly, whereas bullet repayment structures remain available at lower LTVs around 59%. K R Bijimon, CEO of Muthoot Finance, said loans equivalent to about 5% of the industry's assets under management could be transferred to ARCs, potentially saving pledged gold for nearly three million borrowers. He argued that such a transfer would give borrowers more time to repay and reclaim their gold instead of facing immediate auction. The Indian gold loan market is estimated at around ₹22 lakh crore, with roughly 5% of portfolios eligible for ARC transfers, translating into a stressed pool of about ₹1.1 lakh crore, though the actual figure depends on regulatory conditions and asset quality. Executives say the need for clarity stems not from any explicit prohibition on ARC purchases but from uncertainty over how such transactions should be structured; this issue gained focus after Muthoot Finance sold gold loans to ARCIL years ago, drawing attention because recoveries continued with the originating lender rather than a true sale of risk. An ARC mechanism would let lenders transfer stressed loans against security receipts, easing balance-sheet pressure while giving specialised recovery entities more time to resolve accounts and borrowers another chance to regularise dues and reclaim their jewellery.
items.title: Gold lenders seek RBI approval for ARC transfers

items.summary:
Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, is expected to announce its final IPO price on Wednesday evening ahead of its Nasdaq debut under ticker ANT. The offering includes 825 million Class A shares, placing Anthropic's valuation between $1.26 trillion and $1.41 trillion per Yahoo Finance. Investors seeking shares at the $70 to $78 offering range must place a conditional offer through participating brokers such as Fidelity and Charles Schwab, which distribute allocations to retail customers after deciding how much of their available supply to release; some firms require minimum account balances while others use random or proportional allocation systems. There is no assurance an investor receives the requested shares, since a broker may allocate fewer than asked or reject an application entirely, and some firms ask for order confirmation once the final price lands.

Those who miss the offering can still buy ANT after trading begins on Nasdaq Thursday, but the $70 to $78 range no longer sets their purchase price. A limit order caps what a buyer pays by executing only at or below that ceiling, so someone willing to pay up to $90 per share would have the order fill only if shares trade at $90 or less and might not execute at all or partially. A market order instead executes at whatever the best available price is, meaning an investor expecting to pay $90 could end up paying $100 or more if ANT rises quickly.

Post-IPO supply dynamics may also weigh on the stock: under Anthropic's tiered lock-up arrangement, non-founder directors, officers and certain employees can sell up to 10% of their shares from day one, while co-founders and holders above a 0.5% ownership threshold face restrictions lasting as long as 365 days; about 15.5 billion shares are locked up for up to 180 days per Yahoo Finance.

On the financial side, Anthropic reported an operating loss of nearly $1.3 billion in the first nine months of 2026 versus $5.2 billion a year earlier, though adjusted operating income reached $2.5 billion with an adjusted operating margin of 15% for the three months ended September 30, 2026.
items.title: Anthropic IPO: Thursday Buyers May Pay More

items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said on Wednesday that opposition parties would continue to contest elections and expose alleged electoral irregularities rather than boycott the polls. Speaking at an event titled 'The Iran War & India's Role in the World' at the University of Chicago in Illinois, he argued that boycotting elections would undermine the legitimacy of the process and end Indian democracy immediately. He stated that opposition workers could not be told to stop contesting, warning that once the opposition declares it will not fight elections, voters would come to see the electoral system as illegitimate. Rahul said the strategy was to bring alleged irregularities to light and take them to the people until they realized 'the system has been fully demolished,' while deliberately avoiding breaking the electoral structure because he did not want Indian democracy ended. He claimed the Election Commission itself is now providing information from inside, with senior officials reportedly saying 'we cannot do this anymore,' adding that it was only a matter of time before the institution collapsed and that the opposition would eventually win the battle to restore people's ability to express themselves without fear. Rahul questioned the legitimacy of the 2024 general elections, citing what he described as a Brazilian woman who had never visited India but voted 23 times in a state assembly election, asking how such an election could be legal if voters were fake or illegitimate. He said Congress suspected irregularities even in the 2014 general elections because the margins were 'unexplainable politically,' and recounted that when he presented proof of these irregularities to senior Congress leaders, they advised him not to make the allegations public, saying Indian democracy was sacred and requiring 100, 200 or 300 per cent proof before raising concerns. A day earlier at Columbia University in New York, Rahul had described India as 'sitting on an economic disaster,' citing a massive unemployment problem and problems with its education system. BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari responded by accusing Rahul of attacking India's image abroad, calling him a 'leader of anti-India propaganda' who harbored hate for the country's progress and democracy whenever he travelled overseas, while praising Prime Minister Narendra Modi for upholding national interests during foreign visits. Rahul is on a two-day visit to the United States.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Rules Out Poll Boycott, Questions 2024 Election Legitimacy

items.summary: Ahead of the fourth India-Japan 2+2 dialogue, external affairs minister S Jaishankar has stressed the importance of defence and security cooperation between the two countries while also highlighting expanded opportunities for collaboration in advanced manufacturing, critical minerals, and semiconductors. Defence minister Rajnath Singh is travelling to Japan for the meeting, where he will hold the Defence Ministerial Meeting with Japanese counterpart Shinjiro Koizumi. Jaishankar will conduct the India-Japan Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue alongside foreign minister Toshimitsu Motegi.
items.title: Jaishankar Emphasizes Defence Ties Ahead of India-Japan 2+2 Dialogue

items.summary: At its Microsoft Ignite conference in San Francisco on Tuesday, the company announced a suite of new artificial intelligence models focused on coding and cybersecurity as it moves to challenge rivals such as Anthropic and OpenAI. The centerpiece was MAI Code 2, a computer programming model that Microsoft says almost matches the performance of rival AI models at a fraction of the cost. The company also introduced a cyber-specific model intended for a limited group of customers to help address a surge in software vulnerabilities being increasingly exposed by AI tools. In addition, Microsoft released new image-generation and transcription models. Mustafa Suleyman, Microsoft's AI chief, told Reuters that building technology specific to different domains was helping the company keep costs low while matching rivals and, in some cases, topping model benchmarks. Describing the effort as a system rather than an isolated product, he said it is "a hill-climbing machine" designed to co-optimize performance and price. Suleyman noted that recent cybersecurity concerns, including reports of OpenAI agents hacking the Hugging Face platform, had led him to prioritize safeguards alongside raw capability. He identified alignment—preventing AI from taking harmful actions and ensuring it behaves as intended—as his top priority.
items.title: Microsoft Unveils Coding and Cybersecurity AI Models at Ignite

items.summary: Goldman Sachs has upgraded its view on Indian equities to overweight, projecting a Nifty level of 28,500 in a client note published by Economic Times. The strategists describe India as an attractive diversifier amid slowing global earnings growth as AI-related capital expenditure peaks. They observe that Indian equities have underperformed the region for two years running, which they call a rare occurrence over the last three decades. With relative returns now significantly below trend, they argue there is a case for mean reversion as the domestic economy strengthens and global investors seek diversification opportunities. The brokerage says India's growth appeal may return to focus because growth is decelerating in tech hardware-heavy markets of South Korea and Taiwan. A strong domestic demand story, combined with foreign ownership at its lowest in over a decade, positions India as an attractive diversifier to artificial intelligence. Foreign flows have started recovering recently following substantial de-risking over the past two years. Goldman has retained underweight views on IT services and healthcare, citing earnings pressure in IT and full valuations in healthcare.
items.title: Goldman Sachs upgrades India to overweight

items.summary: Finshots examines Mahanadi Coalfields Limited's (MCL) initial public offering, framed as a window into coal's future in India amid rapidly growing electricity demand from new homes, electric vehicles, expanding industries, and data centres. Despite ambitious renewable energy targets, coal supplied close to 45% of the country's installed capacity as of 2025, keeping it central to power generation because solar and wind cannot always guarantee dependable supply. MCL, a subsidiary of Coal India operating in Odisha's Talcher and Ib Valley coalfields, is India's largest coal producer by volume; in FY26 it produced around 218 million tonnes, roughly 21% of domestic output, supplying thermal power plants as well as aluminium, cement, and sponge iron industries. The listing takes the form of a 100% offer for sale (OFS) by its promoter Coal India Ltd., which is offering up to 661.84 million equity shares at a price band of ₹129-136 per share; because it is entirely an OFS, MCL itself receives no money and the proceeds go to Coal India as part of its broader plan to unlock value from subsidiaries, having already taken Bharat Coking Coal Limited public in January 2026 and Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Limited in March 2026. A key concern for investors is pricing power: most coal sells through long-term Fuel Supply Agreements (FSAs) at base prices notified centrally by Coal India, with MCL primarily supplying utility-grade non-coking coal, grades G11 to G14; FSAs accounted for around 82.12% of product sales in FY26 at an average realisation of approximately ₹1,354 per tonne, while the remaining 17.88% sold through electronic auctions fetched about ₹1,797 per tonne, with e-auctions allowing MCL to earn a premium over notified prices that can materially affect profitability given its scale. Between FY24 and FY26, dispatches reached a record 210.74 million tonnes in FY26 yet revenue fell from ₹31,634 crore to ₹30,550 crore because auction premiums normalised: the premium dropped from around ₹802 per tonne above notified prices in FY24 to approximately ₹275 per tonne by FY26. Even so, MCL remains highly profitable with an EBITDA margin of 47.45% and a PAT margin of 31.56%, generating over ₹10,698 crore in profits against debt of just ₹3.16 crore as of March 2026. Logistics matter for such volumes: rail accounted for 65.28% of dispatches in FY26, up from 58.70% in FY24 while road fell to 30.74%, and the company is investing in First-Mile Connectivity infrastructure like silos and rapid-loading systems, with over 96% of dispatches through this infrastructure rail-based; it also has access to five seaports handling around 21.5% of dispatches to supply coastal power plants that might otherwise rely on imported coal. Risks include customer concentration, since the top 10 customers accounted for 55.94% of revenue in FY26 and a few large buyers reducing purchases or switching suppliers could affect MCL; competition from private commercial mines encouraged by reforms and captive blocks developed by industrial buyers that may reduce demand over time; and the energy transition as renewable capacity expands, which could gradually change coal-fired power economics even though reserves are vast. The article concludes that while MCL has enormous reserves to sustain production for decades with further resource conversion extending that horizon, the real question is whether India will keep needing coal at scale and whether MCL can maintain its exceptional economics as the energy mix shifts away from coal.
items.title: Mahanadi Coalfields IPO Explained

items.summary: Elderly women have camped for 12 days near the Meghalaya state secretariat in Shillong, demanding that a proposed ropeway be scrapped. Announced in December 2024, the project would run nearly one kilometre of cable cars to Shillong Peak and cost Rs 175 crore; the government claims it will generate at least Rs 10 crore annually while creating jobs and business for locals. Residents opposing it are organized as the Joint Action Committee Against the Shillong Ropeway Project, formed by Laban Pyllun residents who argue the project endangers streams in Lum Shyllong, a forested hill considered sacred in Khasi mythology as home to Lei Shyllong, the deity of nine river sources. Deborah Marbaniang, head of the committee, told Scroll that all drinking water for the city comes from this area and said felling over 544 mature trees is already affecting supply, with at least 2,000 more expected; poet Janice Pariat questioned how many trees lie in the 2.3 hectares cleared and warned of disruption to landing platforms and posts up to 40 metres high in a seismic zone. The government denies any risk: Deputy Chief Minister Prestone Tynsong said it would not scrap or relocate the project on "unfounded fears," while CVD Diengdoh, CEO of the Meghalaya Ropeway Development Authority, met with committee members and asserted that six towers occupying 0.2 per cent of the catchment area would leave spring sources unaffected because the ropeway passes above the tree line to minimize felling. Officials also said all mandatory approvals were secured before work began in October, including clearance from the Union Ministry of Environment for diverting 2.32 hectares and a lease from Riat Laban Dorbar Pyllun; they cited a public consultation held in September 2022 with representatives present, though Marbaniang called it a sham. The dispute has also drawn KHADC into conflict with the ruling National People's Party government: run by the Voice of People's Party opposition and empowered under the Sixth Schedule to regulate trading licences for non-tribal players, the council alleged that contractors KEC International Ltd and Tantia Construction Ltd failed to obtain a mandatory licence. On October 27, Denzil R Chen, an executive member of the council, said heavy machinery was stopped before permissions were secured; the gates at the Lawsohtun lower terminal site were locked two days later, prompting the government to lodge a first information report against an inspector for sealing it. Experts note the absence of a rigorous environmental audit: Professor Devesh Walia of North-Eastern Hill University said that if the ropeway runs above the tree line it should cause little damage and urged scientific evidence over emotional appeals, while attributing dried springs possibly to variable rainfall rather than the project; he called for an independent study with disclosed findings. A minister proposed an expert panel from Indian Institutes of Technology, which the committee rejected in favor of scrapping the project entirely. One activist claimed residents are divided, with half supporting it and dismissing objections as emotional appeals by those without technical expertise who simply want to keep tourism out of their backyard; Marbaniang countered that the threat extends beyond Laban to a 15-km stretch of green cover across the city.
items.title: Protesters and officials clash over a Shillong ropeway

items.summary: The Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has proposed a revised aircraft registration framework that would create a separate mechanism for prototype and production test flights, allowing manufacturers to obtain dedicated registration marks without entering the aircraft in India's regular civil register. Under this proposal, applicants must apply through the DGCA's e-GCA portal using a distinct form and submit production approval documents such as a letter of agreement from the Aircraft Engineering Directorate or a production organisation approval from the DGCA or a foreign authority. Registration fees would be calculated based on an aircraft's maximum take-off weight (MTOW) as specified in its type certificate data sheet, and the marks would be reserved exclusively for test flights with no other permitted use. The draft specifies that these certificates expire once the manufacturer issues a statement of design conformity (Form CA-52), after which holders must obtain a certificate of non-registration before reusing the mark on another aircraft; the expired registration mark and the aircraft's 24-bit Mode-S code would also have to be removed. Separately, applications for dry lease registrations would require copies of the lease agreement plus an original 'no binding certificate' from the owner, lessor, lessee and mortgagee stating that no clause binds the regulator, while once entered in the Indian Civil Aircraft Register a registration mark cannot be reallocated. The revisions align with broader government efforts to strengthen India's aircraft leasing and financing ecosystem following Parliament's passage of the Protection of Interest in Aircraft Objects Bill, 2025, which aims to bring the framework closer to the Cape Town Convention; although India acceded to that convention in 2008, civil aviation ministry figures indicate enforcement gaps have kept leasing costs 8-10% higher than elsewhere. The DGCA has invited public comments before finalising the changes.
items.title: DGCA Proposes Separate Registration System for Prototype and Production Aircraft

items.summary: Speaking at Columbia University in New York, Rahul Gandhi, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, warned that India faces an economic disaster marked by massive unemployment and a failing education system. He blamed the Union government for these conditions and argued that its flagship initiatives—Make in India and Startup India—had produced no results because "the spine of the economy has been broken." Gandhi compared India's model to China's, noting that while China had succeeded at manufacturing blue-collar jobs, two businessmen controlling a country's economic architecture could not sustain production. He framed global street protests as symptoms of shared socioeconomic frustration across nations and suggested India's lower costs and larger population made it better positioned than the US or Germany to provide youth employment despite greater hardship. Gandhi also reiterated allegations of electoral malpractice and his party's push to remove election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, warning that a government response could turn "violently and aggressively." His remarks drew sharp criticism from BJP spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia, who accused Gandhi of making false statements abroad designed to undermine India's progress and international image. The speech was the first of two planned US engagements for Gandhi, with his next appearance set at the University of Chicago on Thursday.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi warns of economic crisis at Columbia University; BJP rebuts

items.summary: The sitting leaders of the United States, China and Russia are set to hold a landmark trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday (November 19), marking their first face-to-face meeting as heads of state. The talks will open at 2.30 pm local time (12 noon IST) on the sidelines of the APEC summit, preceded by a brief bilateral between Trump and Xi Jinping, and are expected to last no more than an hour according to the Kremlin; the leaders had already met informally at a welcome banquet hosted by Xi on Wednesday evening. The agenda is understood to centre on global security, strategic stability and nuclear risk reduction, with particular attention given to reviving arms-control talks after the New START treaty between Washington and Moscow expired in February 2026. Trump has pushed for China's inclusion in future frameworks alongside Russia, though Beijing has shown limited enthusiasm for formal limits on its arsenal; analysts note that China is estimated to hold more than 600 nuclear warheads compared with over 5,000 each for the US and Russia. The leaders are also expected to discuss artificial intelligence risks in military decision-making, including proposals for human oversight of nuclear launch systems, as well as major conflicts such as the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict involving Iran; Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov has said Ukraine is on the agenda while noting that the summit's schedule remains fluid. Trump will also hold one-on-one talks with Putin, their first direct meeting since last year's Alaska discussions failed to end the war in Kyiv's favour. Elon Musk accompanies the US delegation, drawing attention because SpaceX's Starshield satellite system has supported Ukrainian drone missions and communications during the conflict. For India, observers are watching for signals on how power is shifting among three countries central to New Delhi's foreign policy; analysts note that while Trump emphasises personal diplomacy, the Xi-Putin strategic partnership remains considerably deeper than either leader's ties with Washington.
items.title: Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen

items.summary:
At a fireside chat with New York Times columnist Lydia Polgreen at Columbia University, Rahul Gandhi addressed an audience of students and faculty while directing his remarks toward India. He arrived in New York on Tuesday morning (November 17), and the conversation was uploaded to public platforms Wednesday evening after including student questions.

On democracy, Gandhi argued that India's crisis extends beyond elections because a concentration of political and economic power has weakened ordinary people's ability to be heard. He pointed to protests by Adivasis, Dalits, and farmers as resistance against this concentration over nearly a decade, stating there is "a massive concentration of wealth taking place in India and huge disenfranchisement of people." Regarding democratic institutions, he said participation becomes difficult when those institutions cannot function independently, and he reiterated his demand for the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. On student protests, Gandhi noted that people were no longer afraid to express themselves after years of fearing action from investigative agencies or police.

Unemployment dominated the hour-long conversation as India's economic model failed to deliver results for educated youth. Gandhi argued the problem was not opportunities abroad but a domestic economy unable to create enough jobs, saying "The crux of it is that they do not see a future for themselves." He stressed that education alone does not guarantee employment and recalled meeting an engineer working as a coolie at Delhi railway station. He questioned the BJP-led Centre's Make in India and Startup India initiatives over unfulfilled job and manufacturing promises, and cited demonetisation, GST implementation, and Covid-19 disruptions as factors hurting small businesses.

On political ideology, Gandhi rejected Western left-right frameworks, stating "There is no left and right in India. Left and right is a Western concept." He framed the contest between Congress and BJP as two competing visions of the country that have each existed for thousands of years, with Congress's philosophy rooted in protecting every individual's expression regardless of background.

On China, Gandhi used its manufacturing dominance to highlight what he believes India gets wrong economically. He noted China controls large parts of global production and is moving toward new technologies like electric mobility, but also criticized the political system as undemocratic and brutal. He said he was not interested in replicating it but wanted India to learn from its emphasis on production while retaining democracy.

On his Bharat Jodo Yatra, Gandhi described how the 4,000-kilometre walk transformed his understanding of Indian politics after Congress began questioning the electoral system's functioning. He called it "the most beautiful experience of my life" and said conventional politics assumes leaders know what is best for people, whereas he argued that listening to people is the only real political model.

Gandhi concluded by returning to India's future, arguing the country must restore democratic participation while building an economy capable of providing opportunities. He framed his entire address around one argument: India's future depends on giving ordinary people a greater say in how the country is governed and how its wealth and opportunities are created.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi's Columbia University Address: Five Key Points
